title: Jude and the Oath Revisited
premise: Casper Dunmore, a bone-carver who hears the dead and keeps the ledgers of a guild trading in impossible things, has survived by being unremarkable in a city built on forgetting. When a child arrives speaking a language that predates kingdoms, Casper recognizes it as the tongue of Vell, the drowned country her own family erased themselves from to survive its fall. The ledgers reveal the guild has been quietly buying up pieces of Vell—doors, names, bones—and sealing them away so no one can go home again. To save the child from the guild's collectors, Casper must reopen one of those doors, confront the memory of what her ancestors did to earn their survival, and choose between erasing herself as they did or carrying Vell's language forward. In the end she walks the child through the last door into the country that no longer exists, stays behind as its keeper of ledgers, and lets her own name be forgotten so the old tongue can be remembered.
about_author: Tamsin Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing the belongings of families who fled vanished places. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things everyone else agrees to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Bones
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the guildhouse of impossible things, Casper carves a memorial bead for a dead ferryman while the guild's collectors argue over inventory. She hears his ghost correcting her measurements. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; we learn she survives by making herself useful and invisible.

chapters.title: A Child at the Ledger Door
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A mud-soaked child appears at the guild door speaking a language no collector can place—and Casper understands every word. It is Vellish, the tongue of the drowned country, and hearing it unlocks memories she didn't know she had. Emotional beat: recognition and dread arriving together.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Bought
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Digging through sealed volumes, Casper finds the guild's oldest accounts: doors purchased, names bought and burned, whole villages of Vell erased by contract—including, on one page, her own grandmother's name. Beat: the sickening discovery that invisibility was a transaction, not an accident.

chapters.title: The Collector's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Maren Hale, chief collector. Maren suspects the child is contraband memory and offers Casper protection in exchange for silence, revealing the guild fears a 'reopening.' Casper lies for the first time in years. Beat: the seductive comfort of complicity, and how easily survival becomes betrayal.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dying Tongue
chapters.summary: POV alternating Casper and the child, Ilo. Hiding in the bone-cellar, Casper teaches Ilo carved words while Ilo teaches her songs the dead begin humming along to. The ghosts grow restless, hungry for their language. Beat: tenderness blooming inside danger, and grief with nowhere to go.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the River
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Following ledger clues and the ferryman's ghost, Casper locates a sealed Vellish door beneath the river pilings—but it is warded against exactly her kind: descendants who traded their names away. The ward asks a question in Vellish she cannot honestly answer. Beat: hope meeting its price.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Unremarkable
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Maren confronts Casper with evidence of the lie, and offers a final bargain: surrender the child, receive a new name, true anonymity forever. Casper sees her whole future laid out—a long, safe, empty life. Beat: the temptation of erasure made explicit and almost irresistible.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Among the burned-name contracts Casper finds her grandmother's confession: the family survived Vell's fall by informing on neighbors, buying their erasure with others' deaths. Her grandmother's ghost arrives to confirm it, begging forgiveness or silence. Beat: identity shattered—the price of survival was never abstract.

chapters.title: The Question at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Casper, climax. With collectors closing in, Casper carries Ilo to the river door. The ward repeats its question: 'Who are you?' Instead of lying or claiming innocence, Casper answers with the truth—her grandmother's crime, her own complicity, her real name spoken aloud in Vellish. The door opens. Beat: honesty as the only key.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Forgotten Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Casper, resolution. Casper sends Ilo through into Vell—not to a restored country but to its memory, where the language can live—and chooses to stay as the door's keeper, asking the guild to strike her name from every book. The ghosts sing. Beat: bittersweet peace; she loses her name and finally gains herself.
